transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you’d like to talk about?

Well, hello, Doctor. Thank you for having me. I suppose... well, my daughter was the one who insisted I come in. She’s a lovely girl, always fussing over me. Just last week she brought over a casserole—chicken and rice, you know, the kind my late wife used to make. She tried her best, but she always puts a bit too much salt in it. Anyway, what brings me in... yes. It's... it's the bridges. The moment I know a bridge crossing is unavoidable, my heart just starts pounding out of my chest. My hands get all damp on the steering wheel, or the armrest if someone else is driving, and I feel this terrible rush of fear before we're even on the thing. It’s dreadful. I remember when they built the new overpass near the old grocery store—the one that closed down back in '98, I think it was. Used to buy my cigars there. But yes, the bridges... just thinking about having to cross one makes me feel like I'm going to jump out of my own skin.
When you feel this fear on bridges, is it specifically about being on the bridge itself, or does it also happen in other places like open roads, crowded areas, or other public spaces?

Oh, no, no. Open roads are fine. Beautiful, really. My late wife and I, we used to drive all the way out west back in the late sixties. We had this old Ford, sky blue, ran like an absolute top. The open roads back then felt so free, you know? And crowds don't bother me either. I was just at a big street fair a few years ago with my daughter. Packed like sardines, but it was wonderful. They had this fellow playing the trombone, and I used to play the trombone in high school, actually. I wasn't half bad, either! 

But, uh... what were we saying? Right, the places. No, it's really just the bridges. I mean, I know perfectly well that thousands of cars cross those bridges every single day. I'm a rational man, I read the engineering articles in the paper. But... well, when I see a high span on the map, or if I spot it looming ahead through the windshield, it just... it feels to me as if the whole thing is waiting to drop away right from under us. Just collapse straight into the river. It's a terrifying feeling. Did you know the river downtown is over eighty feet deep in some parts? Frightening to think about. But yes, just the bridges.

latest_inference.note: The patient specifically describes an intense, irrational fear of bridges, which does not extend to other situations such as open roads or crowded areas. This rules out Agoraphobia (F40.110), other phobias (F40.210, F40.230), and general Anxiety Disorder (F41.9). The fear is bridge-specific, which falls under 'Other specified phobias' (F40.290).

The differential includes phobias related to heights (acrophobia), enclosed spaces (claustrophobia), or bridges specifically (which may fall under 'other specified phobias'). Agoraphobia and general anxiety disorder are also possible but less specifically supported at this point.
